--- output ---
1	"""Contrastive Correction Memory.
2	
3	Prior systems show the model WHAT the right answer looks like. This system
4	also shows it WHAT NOT TO DO: before the examples, it injects a
5	"Mistakes to avoid" section built from stored wrong-prediction records.
6	
7	Mechanism:
8	1. learn_from_batch stores all examples in a retrieval pool (as usual), but
9	   also stores wrong predictions as correction records:
10	       (input_tokens, wrong_prediction, correct_label)
11	
12	2. At predict time:
13	   a. Retrieve top-k similar corrections by bigram Jaccard similarity.
14	   b. Format them into a "Mistakes to avoid" block placed BEFORE the examples.
15	   c. Fill the remaining context budget with standard similarity-ranked examples.
16	
17	Why this helps: the model already "knows" Chinese criminal law from pretraining.
18	What it gets wrong is fine-grained label disambiguation — predicting "诈骗" when
19	the correct answer is "合同诈骗", or "行贿" when it is "单位行贿". Surfacing
20	the exact wrong→right mappings from semantically similar cases directly
21	addresses those boundary errors without relying on the confusion matrix
22	(which requires multiple errors on the same pair to accumulate signal).
23	
24	This changes both the memory content (B) and the prompt architecture (A),
25	making it a genuine dual-axis exploration candidate.
26	"""
27	
28	import json
29	import re
30	from collections import defaultdict
31	from typing import Any
32	
33	from ..llm import LLMCallable
34	from ..memory_system import MemorySystem, extract_json_field
35	
36	# ── prompt template ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
37	
38	PROMPT_TEMPLATE = """Solve the problem below based on the examples and correction guidance provided.
39	
40	{corrections_section}{examples_section}
41	
42	**Problem:**
43	{input}
44	
45	**Instructions:**
46	- Follow the patterns shown in the examples above
47	- Pay attention to the mistakes listed above — avoid the same errors for similar cases
48	- Respond in JSON format
49	
50	{{"reasoning": "[your reasoning]", "final_answer": "[your answer]"}}"""
51	
52	CORRECTIONS_HEADER = """**Mistakes to avoid** (from similar cases in memory):
53	{correction_lines}
54	
55	"""
56	
57	MAX_CHARS = 30000
58	# Maximum corrections to inject (each is short, so budget is mainly examples)
59	_MAX_CORRECTIONS = 4
60	# Minimum similarity for a correction to be considered relevant
61	_MIN_CORRECTION_SIM = 0.02
62	# Examples to fill after corrections
63	_MAX_EXAMPLES = 20
64	
65	
66	# ── tokenizer (Chinese bigrams + ASCII) ──────────────────────────────────────
67	
68	def _tokenize(text: str) -> frozenset[str]:
69	    tokens: set[str] = set()
70	    tokens.update(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", text.lower()))
71	    cjk_chars = re.findall(r"[一-鿿]", text)
72	    for i in range(len(cjk_chars) - 1):
73	        tokens.add(cjk_chars[i] + cjk_chars[i + 1])
74	    return frozenset(tokens)
75	
76	
77	def _jaccard(a: frozenset[str], b: frozenset[str]) -> float:
78	    if not a and not b:
79	        return 0.0
80	    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)
81	
82	
83	# ── memory system ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84	
85	class ContrastiveCorrectionMemory(MemorySystem):
86	    """Error-contrastive memory: injects wrong→right pairs as negative guidance."""
87	
88	    def __init__(self, llm: LLMCallable):
89	        super().__init__(llm)
90	        # Standard example pool for retrieval
91	        self.examples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
92	        # Correction records: {tokens, wrong, right, input_preview}
93	        self.corrections: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
94	
95	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
96	    # Retrieval helpers
97	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
98	
99	    def _top_corrections(self, q_tok: frozenset[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
100	        scored = [
101	            (c, _jaccard(q_tok, c["tokens"]))
102	            for c in self.corrections
103	        ]
104	        # Filter by minimum relevance, then sort descending
105	        relevant = [(c, s) for c, s in scored if s >= _MIN_CORRECTION_SIM]
106	        relevant.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
107	        return [c for c, _ in relevant[:_MAX_CORRECTIONS]]
108	
109	    def _top_examples(self, q_tok: frozenset[str]) -> list[tuple[float, int, dict]]:
110	        scored = [
111	            (_jaccard(q_tok, ex["tokens"]), idx, ex)
112	            for idx, ex in enumerate(self.examples)
113	        ]
114	        scored.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]), reverse=True)
115	        return scored
116	
117	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
118	    # Prompt assembly
119	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
120	
121	    def _build_prompt(self, input_text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
122	        q_tok = _tokenize(input_text)
123	        total_chars = 0
124	
125	        # --- Corrections block ---
126	        corrections = self._top_corrections(q_tok)
127	        corr_lines: list[str] = []
128	        for c in corrections:
129	            line = f"- For cases like: \"{c['preview']}\" — predicted \"{c['wrong']}\", correct answer is \"{c['right']}\""
130	            corr_lines.append(line)
131	            total_chars += len(line) + 1
132	
133	        if corr_lines:
134	            corrections_section = CORRECTIONS_HEADER.format(
135	                correction_lines="\n".join(corr_lines)
136	            )
137	        else:
138	            corrections_section = ""
139	
140	        # --- Examples block ---
141	        ranked = self._top_examples(q_tok)
142	        parts: list[str] = []
143	        used: set[int] = set()
144	
145	        for _, idx, ex in ranked:
146	            if idx in used:
147	                continue
148	            q = ex.get("raw_question", ex["input"])
149	            part = f"Q: {q}\nA: {ex['target']}"
150	            if total_chars + len(part) + 2 > MAX_CHARS:
151	                break
152	            parts.append(part)
153	            used.add(idx)
154	            total_chars += len(part) + 2
155	            if len(parts) >= _MAX_EXAMPLES:
156	                break
157	
158	        examples_section = "\n\n".join(parts)
159	        if parts:
160	            examples_section = "**Examples:**\n" + examples_section + "\n\n"
161	
162	        return corrections_section, examples_section, len(parts), len(corrections)
163	
164	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
165	    # MemorySystem interface
166	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
167	
168	    def predict(self, input: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
169	        corrections_section, examples_section, n_examples, n_corrections = self._build_prompt(input)
170	        prompt = PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(
171	            corrections_section=corrections_section,
172	            examples_section=examples_section,
173	            input=input,
174	        )
175	        response = self.call_llm(prompt)
176	        answer = extract_json_field(response, "final_answer")
177	        return answer, {
178	            "full_response": response,
179	            "num_examples": len(self.examples),
180	            "num_selected": n_examples,
181	            "num_corrections": n_corrections,
182	            "num_correction_pool": len(self.corrections),
183	        }
184	
185	    def learn_from_batch(self, batch_results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
186	        for r in batch_results:
187	            raw_q = r.get("raw_question", r["input"])
188	            tok = _tokenize(raw_q)
189	            ex: dict[str, Any] = {
190	                "input": r["input"],
191	                "target": r["ground_truth"],
192	                "tokens": tok,
193	            }
194	            if "raw_question" in r:
195	                ex["raw_question"] = r["raw_question"]
196	            self.examples.append(ex)
197	
198	            # Store correction records for wrong predictions
199	            if not r.get("was_correct", True):
200	                pred = r.get("prediction", "")
201	                gt = r["ground_truth"]
202	                if pred and pred != gt:
203	                    # Truncate preview to ~60 chars for prompt compactness
204	                    preview = raw_q[:60].replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", "")
205	                    self.corrections.append({
206	                        "tokens": tok,
207	                        "wrong": pred,
208	                        "right": gt,
209	                        "preview": preview,
210	                    })
211	
212	    def get_state(self) -> str:
213	        ex_serial = [
214	            {k: (sorted(v) if isinstance(v, frozenset) else v) for k, v in ex.items()}
215	            for ex in self.examples
216	        ]
217	        corr_serial = [
218	            {k: (sorted(v) if isinstance(v, frozenset) else v) for k, v in c.items()}
219	            for c in self.corrections
220	        ]
221	        return json.dumps({"examples": ex_serial, "corrections": corr_serial}, indent=2)
222	
223	    def set_state(self, state: str) -> None:
224	        data = json.loads(state)
225	        self.examples = []
226	        for ex in data.get("examples", []):
227	            restored = dict(ex)
228	            if "tokens" in restored and isinstance(restored["tokens"], list):
229	                restored["tokens"] = frozenset(restored["tokens"])
230	            else:
231	                raw_q = restored.get("raw_question", restored.get("input", ""))
232	                restored["tokens"] = _tokenize(raw_q)
233	            self.examples.append(restored)
234	
235	        self.corrections = []
236	        for c in data.get("corrections", []):
237	            restored = dict(c)
238	            if "tokens" in restored and isinstance(restored["tokens"], list):
239	                restored["tokens"] = frozenset(restored["tokens"])
240	            self.corrections.append(restored)
241
